Nov 21 : The Confederation of African Football (CAF) announced on Saturday a return to profitability for the 2025-26 financial year with a net surplus of $31.2 million and increased total revenue of $284 million. • The announcement was made at CAF's 48th Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, Nigeria • CAF’s revenue was boosted by the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco, where a record 23 commercial partners helped to generate more than $100 million for the organisation • CAF's reserves also improved from a deficit of $16.8 million to a positive position of $14.4 million, while its cash balance position as of the year ended June 2026 stood at $118.8 million

FAST

PORTIMAO, Portugal, Nov 21 : Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi took pole position for the Portuguese Grand Prix on Saturday, smashing the lap record at the Algarve International Circuit to snatch pole from Ducati's title-chasing Marc Marquez. Marquez initially topped the timesheets in an overcast Q2 session but Bezzecchi stormed to pole with a lap of 1:37.201, nearly half a second quicker than the Spaniard. "Super happy, it wasn't an easy day because the conditions were quite strange, quite tough compared to yesterday (in practice)," Bezzecchi said. "But I felt good. I tried to take some more risk because the qualifying is too important right now and the grid for today and for tomorrow is crucial. So it was important to secure a good qualifying and the pole position is even better."

VR46 Racing's Fabio di Giannantonio will join them on the front row while Aprilia's Jorge Martin, who must ensure Marquez leaves Portugal with no more than a 36-point lead to take the title fight to the final round in Valencia, lines up seventh. Marquez, who can win an eighth MotoGP title if he wins the sprint, leads Martin by 60 points with 74 up for grabs in the final two rounds. Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez was fourth fastest and is joined on the second row by Gresini Racing's Alex Marquez and KTM's Pedro Acosta. Earlier, the Q1 session was red-flagged when Honda's Diogo Moreira suffered a highside crash, with the Brazilian violently thrown off his bike before he landed several metres away, but he escaped any major injury. He was back up on his feet immediately to hitch a ride back to the paddock, safe in the knowledge that his fastest lap was enough to help him advance to Q2 with Ducati's Iker Lecuona, who is standing in for the injured Francesco Bagnaia. "It was a tricky qualifying, especially after a big crash from Moreira... But it's true that on the qualifying, it was time to take a risk," Marquez said. "Why? Because I believe that if we take a risk in the qualifying, we minimise the risk in the sprint and the main race, at least in the first (few) laps." Organisers rescheduled the sprint to 1430 local time, 30 minutes earlier than planned, because forecast poor weather threatened to ground the medical helicopter.

Nov 21 : Confederation of African Football (CAF) president Patrice Motsepe has again endorsed Gianni Infantino for re-election as FIFA President as the Swiss confirmed a huge increase in grant payments to each member association on Saturday.   Speaking at the organisation’s Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, Nigeria, Motsepe said CAF was backing Infantino for another term following challenges from French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association.  "I have experienced over the last five years (as CAF president) his deep commitment. Gianni, you have our support among the 54 member associations of CAF," Motsepe said. Infantino said he would continue to put developing football in Africa at the forefront of his agenda while FIFA president.

"You will always find in me and in FIFA a trusted partner, a trusted brother, to make sure that the dreams that we all have, the dreams that these children have in Abuja, in Cape Town, in Cairo, everywhere in Africa, can become reality," he said. Infantino reiterated the plan to more than triple the grant given to FIFA member associations around the world, from the current $8 million over a four-year period to $25 million. It will be effective from January 2027, three months before the FIFA presidential elections in Morocco.  The plan to increase the grants under the new FIFA Forward 4.0 programme had been mooted in October, and is set to be ratified at a FIFA Council meeting next month. "When I was first elected (in 2016), each federation was receiving from FIFA $250,000 a year, or $1 million every four years for football development," Infantino said. "Now, 10 years later, you will receive $25 million to invest in football development. And we will work to make it even more than that. Because you deserve it. Because your youth deserve it. "FIFA’s money is your money, and you invest it in infrastructure, in development and in opportunities. "We believe in Africa, because we love Africa, because we are Africa," he said to rapturous applause. CONMEBOL on Friday reaffirmed its unanimous support for Infantino's bid for another term, with all 10 member associations of the South American confederation backing his candidacy.

Nov 21 : The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) unveiled on Saturday a revamped central contract structure for 2026-27, expanding the pool of contracted players to 38 from 30, with Salman Ali Agha and Babar Azam the only players placed in the highest category. • The PCB had said in June that only male cricketers who had played at least four tests, six one-day internationals or six Twenty20s in the previous 12 months would be eligible for central contracts. • Under the new system, contracts are split into five specialised categories: tests and ODIs, test specialists, ODIs and T20Is, T20I specialists, and emerging players in the developmental pathway. • The new contracts run through June 30, 2027. Players had been without central contracts since the expiry of the previous cycle in June.

LAS VEGAS, Nov 20 : Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc voiced frustration after neither driver reached the final top-10 phase of qualifying for Saturday night's Las Vegas Formula One Grand Prix. Leclerc was 11th fastest and seven-times world champion Hamilton 12th after struggling for straight-line speed down the floodlit Strip on Friday, though both moved up one spot thanks to McLaren's Oscar Piastri taking a 10-place grid drop. Hamilton said floor damage from debris early in the session had cost him. "We lost a bunch of downforce with it, a few tenths," the Briton said. "Then we lost this deployment and I lost like six tenths just on deployment.

JAKARTA: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) on Saturday (Nov 21) announced sanctions in 10 capital market violation cases, amid efforts to strengthen enforcement, bolster market integrity and protect investors. OJK ordered the return of 23.77 billion rupiah (US$1.3 million) in illicit gains from three stock manipulation cases, involving shares of PT Grand House Mulia, PT Saraswanti Anugerah Makmur and PT Suryamas Dutamakmur. In the Grand House Mulia case, OJK also ordered the closure of 15 securities accounts linked to the trading activity between March and July 2023. The agency also imposed a total of 3.71 billion rupiah in administrative fines on seven listed companies for disclosure failures, material and affiliated-party transaction breaches, financial reporting violations and non-compliance with share transfer obligations. OJK also barred multiple individuals involved in the manipulation cases from participating in Indonesia's capital markets, derivatives and carbon exchange sectors for periods ranging from three to 10 years.  OJK previously sanctioned three listed firms as part of Indonesia's market reforms following concerns raised by global index providers over the transparency and investability of Indonesia's capital markets.

FAST

NEW DELHI: The youth wing of India's main opposition Congress party clashed with police outside Meta offices, protesting the company's removal of some Instagram accounts of its members, according to footage released by the group on Saturday (Nov 21). Meta declined to comment on the protests, an escalation by the influential political group in the company's biggest market by users. Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to remove social media content it objects to. Modi's government says it orders content taken down only if it breaches local laws, can harm public safety or national security. Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi's government. Meta has said it restricts content in India to comply with local laws.

MODI'S PARTY ACCUSES CONGRESS OF VANDALISM Pradeep Bhandari, a national spokesperson for Modi's ruling party, criticised Congress' actions on Saturday, saying they had "not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad" but were also "flaunting it on social media". "This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of Private companies," he wrote. India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. In Hyderabad on Friday, protesters carrying placards chanted slogans as they stormed into the building that houses Meta's offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress' X account. Another video showed Congress workers spray-painting anti-Meta slogans on walls outside the building that houses its Mumbai office, clashing with security guards who tried to stop them.

Police officers detain an Indian Youth Congress member as party members protest against the suspension of their party leaders' accounts at a Meta office building in Hyderabad, Telangana, India on Nov 20, 2026, in this picture screengrab from a social media video. (Screengrab: Reuters via Indian Youth Congress)

In Gurugram near New Delhi, Congress workers chanted slogans and held banners reading "restore youth Congress accounts", official online posts showed. The Indian Youth Congress posted warnings on X that it would "storm your offices across the country and stage protests" unless Instagram accounts of its leaders are restored. Two such accounts were restored after Friday's protests, but thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted, Manu Jain, who is in charge of social media for the youth group, told Reuters on Saturday. Meta must explain how its algorithms restrict posts and must restore accounts taken down on government orders, he added. Reporters Without Borders has said the removal of journalistic content from social media has been on the rise in India this year, and free-speech activists say a new government rule gives social media companies hardly any time to review and decide on takedown requests. In February, Modi's government ordered social media companies to take down unlawful content within three hours of being notified about it, tightening an earlier 36-hour timeline. Meta disclosures show that it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, second only to Indonesia and up from about 70,000 in the preceding six months. "The large majority of these items included instances where we were obligated to proactively restrict content ... based on local law requirements," Meta said.

Nov 20 : Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market value, slid to its lowest level in two years on Friday as worries over stretched valuations in artificial intelligence stocks rattled investors and weighed on other risk assets. It fell 5.10 per cent to $55,830 by 11:13 p.m. ET on Friday (0413 GMT on Saturday), the lowest since September 2024. It was earlier down by 3.57 per cent at $56,813.68. Earlier on Friday it fell below $60,000 for the first time since July.  Crypto markets have been shaken in recent sessions by weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks following Democrats' win in the US midterm elections and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure. The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced "Liberation Day" tariffs.

Source: Reuters

Nov 20 : SoftBank Group CEO Masayoshi Son recently approached Wall Street institutions about financing a possible trillion-dollar "buyout" of South Korean memory chip company SK Hynix, the Information reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The Information quoted a SoftBank spokesperson as saying Son was no longer considering such a deal.  “SoftBank explores many opportunities, and this one is no longer under active consideration,” the report said, citing the spokesperson.  SK Hynix said in a statement it has no knowledge of the matter described in the Information report. It added that any foreign acquisition of the company would require prior government approval under Korean law. A SoftBank spokesperson referred to the statement the company gave to the Information, when Reuters sought a comment.

SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung on Saturday (Nov 21) urged the country to move fast as it competes in the global artificial intelligence (AI) race, as he toured a data centre under construction in the southeastern city of Ulsan. "The whole world is competing right now, and speed is vital," Lee said in a public video of his tour. Data centres are a major source of chip demand, and he hoped the success of the project, built by South Korea's second-largest conglomerate SK Group, would draw further investment from global AI companies, Lee said. SK Group is developing the Ulsan data centre jointly with Amazon Web Services (AWS). The estimated cost is 7 trillion won (US$5.2 billion) until 2029, South Korea's science ministry said last year. Operations are scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said in September that the capacity under construction was an initial 103 megawatt by 2029, with plans to expand it by nearly 900 megawatts in the future. The group is also planning further partnerships with global technology companies as the project progresses, Chey said. On Saturday, President Lee said AI investment had mainly been concentrated around Seoul, and that the Ulsan project showed regional growth was possible. After being told that about 900 people were working at the site, Lee said advanced facilities were short of construction workers and that ministries needed to consider how to train the workforce for building data centres and AI infrastructure.

Source: Reuters/as

LAS VEGAS, Nov 20 : Red Bull's Max Verstappen took pole position for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Friday after newly crowned Formula One champion Kimi Antonelli lapped fastest but dropped to sixth due to a grid penalty. Mercedes' George Russell will share the front row with four-time world champion Verstappen, an appetising prospect after the old foes clashed in final practice, following a chilly floodlit qualifying session in which neither Ferrari driver made it to the final top 10 phase.  McLaren's Lando Norris will start the Saturday night race in third place with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar fourth while Mercedes' Antonelli, who became the youngest ever champion at 20 in Mexico this month, had a five-place engine penalty applied and lines up alongside Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad. “I think we had a solid qualifying. We executed well," said Verstappen, who was helped by his teammate on the famed Strip street circuit, where slipstreaming is a key element, but still finished 0.258 seconds slower than Antonelli.

"My first lap in Q3 was pretty much as good as it can be, just with the tow effect as well around the lap. "I think to be on the front row is very good for us."  RUSSELL DEFIANT AFTER STEWARDS WARN VERSTAPPEN   Verstappen, on pole for the third time this season and 51st of his career, was warned by stewards for driving erratically in final practice when he and Russell made contact. The Briton was unimpressed and revived an old beef between the two. "There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who has started their lap but when you do this you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out, with many drivers and everybody accepts it," said Russell. "And I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. So yeah, somebody's got to stand up to that guy." Russell and Verstappen are fighting to end the season second overall, with the Dutch driver 17 points clear and having the momentum with three races remaining. "I wanted to be on pole but I am probably more pleased with the performance today than I was, let's say, in Mexico a couple of weeks ago when I was on the front row," said Russell in his immediate comments after getting out of the car. "But just timing that out lap, getting the slipstream, was just huge. It was pretty crazy, very similar to what we saw in Monza." Liam Lawson starts seventh for Racing Bulls with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and teammate Franco Colapinto ninth. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc will start 10th after McLaren's Oscar Piastri, seventh fastest in the session, dropped 10 places. Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton will start 11th. Russell was fastest in the first phase with Antonelli second and Leclerc third but Ferrari then suffered a nightmare in Q2. Seven-time champion Hamilton reported a lack of grip after running off track and then struggled to find a tow to get him back up the order from 13th. Neither of us got through?" asked Hamilton over the radio. Verstappen was on provisional pole in the final phase with a lap of one minute 34.151 seconds, well clear of Norris in second and Russell third, after drivers jostled for position with none wanting to go first and provide a tow to those behind. Antonelli only just made it across the line for his final flying lap but posted a best time of 1:33.893. "We thought Kimi was either going to miss the lap or he’s going to be way too close to Lindblad," said Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff. “He crossed the line 1.4 seconds behind, and that was basically it. So, I don’t understand how being that close you can even do this time." (Writing by Alan Baldwin in London, editing by Peter Rutherford)

SYDNEY, Nov 21 : Cricket Australia (CA) backed Pat Cummins to remain as captain of the test and one-day international sides on Saturday and rejected any suggestion his integrity had been compromised amid the renewed furore over the 2018 ball-tampering incident. The board met on Friday and reaffirmed its unanimous support for Cummins, whose leadership has come under scrutiny after Cameron Bancroft, one of three players sanctioned over the Sandpapergate scandal alongside David Warner and Steve Smith, published a detailed account of the incident. CA said the meeting focused on safeguarding the integrity of the game and the welfare of those affected by the 2018 South Africa tour. "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," Cricket Australia Chairman David Boon said in a statement.

The scandal was reignited when former batter Usman Khawaja said knowledge of the ball-tampering plot extended beyond the three players sanctioned by CA's integrity unit. Cummins and his fellow fast bowlers Josh Hazlewood and Mitch Starc have said they knew nothing of the plan. Hazlewood on Saturday reiterated that he did not know a foreign substance was being used on the field. CA attempted to draw a line under the scandal on Wednesday by announcing an independent forum for all the players to give their accounts of what happened in 2018 without fear of sanction. Cummins welcomed the board's support and confirmed he would participate in the process. "Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I have and never will take that lightly," Cummins said. "I support the forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. FAST

GENEVA: Efforts to set firm rules on AI-powered killer robots and drones ran aground on Saturday (Nov 21) as UN-backed talks in Geneva produced a softened agreement to extend discussions for two more years. Scores of countries ended the week-long UN conference on weapons by agreeing to “elaborate” a possible accord on such lethal autonomous weapons systems by 2028. But they did not commit to binding rules sought by UN Secretary-General António Guterres, many countries, and activists. The outcome underscored the difficulty of achieving concrete results in diplomacy amid global conflicts and major military powers jockeying for dominance. Izumi Nakamitsu, the UN high representative for disarmament affairs, hailed a “significant achievement” but acknowledged a “glass half full or half empty” scenario, citing Guterres’ hopes for a legally binding deal this year.

Activists accused military powers like Russia and the United States of blocking stronger language.

A mock "killer robot" is pictured as part of the Campaign to Stop "Killer Robots", which calls for the ban of lethal robot weapons that would be able to select and attack targets without any human intervention. (Photo: AFP/Carl Court)

Stop Killer Robots lamented a “watered-down mandate”, and Beatrice Fihn, founder of international law advocacy group Lex International, said the decision amounts to “pushing the can down the road for two more years". They noted most countries supported work toward a new treaty, and Max Tegmark, a machine learning specialist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and founder of the Future of Life Institute, said: “States have agreed it is sufficient to just talk about the issue, for the 14th year, while these weapons enable atrocities.” Before the meeting, seven countries proposed launching negotiations on a rulebook that could prevent or limit the ability of machines to kill without human control or accountability. That effort fell short. “Technology is moving faster than diplomacy,” said Ambassador Frederico Meyer of Brazil, which joined Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Mexico, New Zealand and Panama in proposing such negotiations. “Diplomats are very slow.” After years of talks on the issue, advocacy groups bemoaned obstructionism largely by Russia, which, like other top AI weapons-developing countries such as the United States, wants a freer hand to develop such high-tech weapons. Guterres, who leaves office at the end of the year, set a 2026 deadline for launching negotiations toward an agreement on autonomous weapons systems. Pope Leo XIV and many advocacy and humanitarian groups have framed the issue as an existential debate, urging quick action to rein in AI weapons before they become too commonplace to regulate easily. Activists say armed drones that can independently strike targets have already been deployed in some select instances in conflict zones, but widespread rollout hasn’t happened. Talks this week centred on the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, ratified by 128 countries, where decisions are made by consensus. That means any single country can thwart an agreement, and that any deal was likely to be based on a low common denominator.
